title: The fake agent's launch record holds the role name next to the arguments
why: A test must check which job werk asked for, and the role travels in the environment, not in the arguments.
body: Each launch of the fake agent records its arguments and the role name from its environment. A test reads the record to check that werk started each kind of agent with the right role and the right request.

title: The control that starts an empty conversation sits in the tab strip, next to the fork control
why: The fork card asks for a second, explicit way to start empty, and the tab strip is where a person already starts a conversation.
body: The tab strip has two controls at its end: '+' forks a conversation at the open card, and a separate control starts a conversation with no parent session. The empty start is never the default of any gesture.

title: werk's agent roles are chat, spec writer, ticket writer, builder, grader, reviewer, classifier, step author and binder
why: Every agent werk starts carries a role, and the fake needs one fixed word per job to pick its reply.
body: Each kind of agent that werk starts has one role name: chat for a conversation, spec writer and ticket writer for the plan, builder for a build pass, grader, reviewer for each of the five review areas, classifier for the overseer's loop check, and step author and binder for the held-out set. The names live in one list of entries. A new kind of agent adds one entry.
